name: Ekenosen

phase_0.boundary_condition: The limit of the unconditioned absolute which contains all self-emptying and filling cycles.

VINIT.justification: The state of absolute potentiality before any act of self-limitation or manifestation occurs.

TANCH.justification: The final state where all emptied elements are gathered into a completed and closed totality.

AFWD.justification: The directed movement of essence from the source toward the other.

AREV.justification: The return of the gift or the descent back into the source through humility.

CLINK.justification: The sequential linking of self-emptying acts that form a continuous history of presence.

IMSCRIB.justification: The recognition that the one who empties is identical to the one who is filled.

FSPLIT.justification: The single essence divides into the Giver and the Gift to facilitate the act of sacrifice.

FFUSE.justification: The Giver and the Gift reunite to reconstitute the original undivided essence.

EVALT.justification: The affirmative state where self-emptying results in the life of the other.

EVALF.justification: The negative state where the lack of self-giving results in isolation.

ENGAGR.justification: The simultaneous state of being completely empty and completely full.

IFIX.justification: The irreversible record of the kenotic act within the history of the absolute.

phase_3.void_description: The silence before the first word of self-expression.
phase_3.true_description: The realization of communion through the act of giving.
phase_3.false_description: The failure to empty the self which leads to ontological stagnation.
phase_3.both_description: The state of the Ekenosen where loss is gain and death is life.

steps.domain_action: The absolute begins in a state of unmanifest potentiality.
The absolute identifies its own nature as the capacity for relation.
The first movement of outpouring initiates the process of manifestation.
The essence divides into the subject who gives and the object which is given.
The T-arm proceeds with the affirmative act of total self-surrender.
The act of surrender links to the reception by the other.
The specific historical moment of the gift is recorded permanently.
The F-arm accounts for the necessary absence and descent required by the gift.
The descent reaches its lowest point to ensure the depth of the kenosis.
The system holds the tension of being both absent in self and present in the other.
The giver and the gift reunite in the shared life of the pleroma.
The absolute recognizes itself as enriched by the cycle of loss.
The system closes as the fullness of the relation is achieved.

phase_5.compiler_frontend: The Volitional Intent which translates the desire for communion into the act of self-limitation.
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: The Perichoretic Flow which allows the exchange of attributes between the giver and the receiver.
phase_5.memory_mechanism: The Eternal Record which preserves every act of sacrifice as a permanent feature of the absolute.
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: The Kairos which determines the precise moment when the emptying must occur for maximum efficacy.
phase_5.alfs_store: The Original Pattern of the self-giving life which serves as the template for all subsequent kenotic acts.

phase_6.cycle_cost: The specific weight of the self-limitation required to create space for the other.
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: A state of undifferentiated and isolated unity.
phase_6.post_cycle_state: A state of differentiated and relational unity.
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The energy lost in the emptying is exactly recovered in the communal filling.
